messages.subject: Spatial recurrent event model
parts:
Dear all,
I am a regular in this group now and I have often found solutions to my problems here. It helps a lot and thanks to all.
I have a problem with a spatial recurrent event model that fails despite my efforts whose formula is:
formula2 <- inla.surv(times14, Status, subject) ~ Trait + Sex + f(Age, model="rw2",scale.model=TRUE) + f(Order, model="ar1") + f(spatial, model=CoxSPDE)

I hope that the nonlinearity of the variable "Age" is well written f(Age, model="rw2", scale.model = TRUE)

In fact, the events (successive infection) at the same individual are correlated between them but I am not sure to have written well the correlation with f(Order, model="ar1"). The variable "Order" is the order of the event in an individual identified by RID.  I wonder if I should write f(RID, model="ar1") or f(RID, control.group = list(model="ar1"))

What would you advise me to do with these formula4 to take into account the nonlinearity of the variable "Age" and the correlation between the infections of the same individual ?

PS: Attached is the output of the model I used

Bests regards

it might be you want ar1 model for Order, but replicated for each
subject, like

f(Order, model="ar1", replicate=subject)

assuming subject=1,2,3... to the number of 'people' in the study.

also Order should be 1,2,3,4...

is this what you want ?

This is exactly what you explained (order=1,2,3.. and subject=ID1, ID2, etc..) but the model does not work with f(Order, model="ar1", replicate=subject). However, it works with f(Order, model="ar1") without the option "replicate".
I specify that we have repeated measurements on individuals (ID), so for the same ID1, we can have more observations at different dates. In fact, the observations are so grouped by ID, shouldn't we write f(ID, model="ar1")? So, the observations of the same ID are correlated, right?

Bests regards

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Spatial recurrent event model
parts:
if you replicate with subject, then subject need to be (numerical)
1,2,3,...

dates: yes, that is your time, you its more

f(dates, model='rw1', replicate=ID)

_but_ you need dates to be the same, equal spaced, and ID to be
numerical 1,2,3..

you might have to use (relative) week number for dates, or something, to
make it managable.

also if you have observations on different weeks, you might need like

f(week, model="ar1", replicate=ID, values=1:52)

say, to define the ar1 to be on 52 weeks, otherwise, it will think
week=1,2,5, is the same as week=1,2,3
